title: [rereview] project-LICHEN-a4n2.3: pop_buf not securely wiped in L2 TX path
description:
Both L2 implementations (firmware/bridge-zephyr/lichen_l2.c:1078 and lichen/subsys/lichen/l2/lichen_l2.c:1576) allocate a stack buffer pop_buf[256] to receive the frame popped from the TX queue. The data (which may contain frame payload) is never securely wiped — it just goes out of scope. On a cooperative RTOS with shallow stack, subsequent function calls may observe the residual frame data.

This is a minor data-leak concern (P3) since the TX path already transmitted this frame over LoRa, so the information is already observable over the air. However, on multi-tenant systems or when sensitive data is being pushed then popped immediately, this could expose frame content to co-located code.

Fix: add secure_wipe(pop_buf, sizeof(pop_buf)) or memset() after the pop call.
